texts: A single coffee plant in the Amsterdam Botanical Garden has been growing continuously since 1700 — making it nearly 325 years old and the oldest known coffee plant in existence, predating the United States by 71 years.

Coffee contains trigonelline, a compound that breaks down into nicotinic acid (vitamin B3) during roasting — this is why coffee contributes a small amount of vitamin B3 to your diet, though you'd need thousands of cups to meet daily requirements.

African penguins use coffee plantations as shelter because the dense leaf canopy mimics their native rocky coastline habitat — some South African farms have become unexpected penguin refuges, with birds nesting between coffee bushes.
